## b7f1df7908e0

**Reproduced distribution defect — canonical analogy support is absent.** The
canonical inputs have profiles `(9, 9, 4)` or `(11, 11, 4)`: the fourth palette
member comes from the filled/hollow example pair in the upper quadrants. In 60
normal generator draws (20 per difficulty band, seed `20261003`, sample indices
`0..19`), all 60 passed `self_check`, but all 60 had palette size 3 and all 60
had zero non-divider colored cells above the divider row. Consequently there
were **0/60 canonical-profile hits**. The independent shared gates reproduce the
same issue: profile floor reports 0/60 exact and envelope hits, and distribution
gate reports `canonical_palette_unreachable: gen=3..3 vs canon=4`.

This leaves training examples without the canonical top-left → top-right analogy
that tells the solver which transformation to transfer to the lower row. A
learner can instead specialize to the generated layout and infer “solid-fill the
lower-left rectangle's bbox in the lower-right,” without ever reading an analogy.
The current rectangular-frame validator cannot refute that specialization.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/b7f1df7908e0/probe_canonical_support.json`
- `checks/audit/b7f1df7908e0/profile_floor/checks/b7f1df7908e0_after_profile_floor.log`
- `checks/audit/b7f1df7908e0/dist_gate/checks/b7f1df7908e0_after_dist_gate.log`

Secondary reproduced blockers, left unchanged as required for an audit target:
the linter reports missing `RULE_HASH`; override checking fails; and no executable
semantic contract is declared. See the corresponding `checks/audit/b7f1df7908e0/`
logs.
